dedupe_keys.name: liquefaction exposure across new zealand state highways

description: This GeoPackage indicates whether liquefaction manifestation is predicted on each New Zealand State Highway link, a road segment between two intersections with another State Highway or a local road. Exposure is binary and is given for six return periods (50, 101, 252, 475, 975 and 2,475 years) and for 388 individual earthquake scenarios. Liquefaction probability comes from a New Zealand modification of the Zhu et al. geospatial model using peak ground velocity, Vs30, precipitation, distance to water and water table depth; shaking comes from the 2022 National Seismic Hazard Model and CyberShake NZ v19.5; a link counts as exposed if any 100 m segment has a probability of at least 0.46. It was produced by Amelia Fabia Lin at the University of Auckland. Coverage is the national State Highway network. Access: free download from Zenodo under CC BY 4.0 (February 2025), in WGS 84. Caveats: exposure is a binary model output, not observed damage, and the threshold drives the result. It supports hazard exposure and road network resilience analysis for earthquakes, and complements the NZTA traffic volumes catalogued here.
